A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same signature-kernel causal-discovery work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V3 reports original simulations of independence testing and causal discovery, functional-data experiments, and a stock-pairs trading study in Section 4 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: V4 retains the original simulation, functional-data, partially observed causal-discovery, and trading results in Section 4 and Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the partially observed extension, and the signature-kernel permutation tests are retained. V4 presents its increment convention as already handled by signature translation invariance; it revises the mathematical description without establishing a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear, nonlinear, path-dependent, and diffusion-dependent SDE settings, missing observations, latent confounding, fractional Brownian motion, functional data, and stock-pairs trading. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: CCM, Granger, PCMCI, SCOTCH, and Lau retain their respective roles. The alternative independence tests in Appendix B.2 and ADF-based trading comparisons in Table 3 are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported sample sizes, graph dimensions, kernel settings, interval choices, baseline training configurations, metrics, and trading split remain unchanged. V4's explanation that whole paths constitute independent samples clarifies the existing setup rather than reporting a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The kernel-bandwidth and interval comparisons, missingness analysis, causal-building-block tests, SCOTCH sensitivity sweep, and case studies are retained. New Appendix A.12 discusses sensitivity to CI-test errors but supplies no new error-analysis or robustness results.

E5.justification: Repeated-instance counts, bootstrap and permutation counts, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Examples include means and standard errors over 40 SDE instances in Table 2, 1000 instances in Figure 3, and 500 settings in Figure 8.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 and v3 appendix Tables 4–9 retain their results, with the latter becoming Tables 5–10. The plotted results also match. For example, Table 3 retains SigKer's return of 0.076 and Sharpe ratio of 1.500; the partially observed experiment retains false-adjacency rates of 88% for SCOTCH and 8% for the proposed method.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces raw path segments in the formal definition with increments X_t−X_a. The Proposition 3.1 proof, moved from A.5 to A.6, correspondingly corrects the independent Brownian inputs, future solution-map output, integration limits, and stochastic integral. New Appendix B.9 adds computational-cost derivations. These are localized mathematical revisions; the principal theorem statements and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: Section 1 replaces the broad claim of exceeding existing methods' scope with an explicit claim to be the first setting simultaneously satisfying four listed capabilities. This refines the novelty claim; the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and guarantees.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.12 explains the difficulty of propagating adaptive CI-test errors into graph-level guarantees and the restricted applicability of existing finite-sample theory. Appendix A.13 clarifies independence across paths, while B.9 identifies computational bottlenecks and the relevance of graph sparsity.

D1.justification: V4 adds clarification of independent path sampling, information about sigkerax versus iisignature and GPU execution, and a reproducibility statement promising future code availability. It supplies no code-release location or evidence of an actual release; existing experimental implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Chevyrev and Kormilitzin (2016) and Morrill et al. (2020) for signature intuition, plus Kalisch and Bühlman (2007) and Spirtes and Meek (1995) for CI-error discussion. Section 1 also sharpens the joint-capability novelty positioning. The broader related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: V4 revises the title and author information, adds a notation overview, explanatory appendix subsections, and reproducibility and funding statements. It also makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds notation Table 4, relocates Figure 3 beside its discussion, clarifies Figure 2's caption, and reflows tables and algorithms. Conference headers and the author layout also change. Existing diagrams and plots are retained, and appendix result tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: V4 improves mathematical precision through the increment formulation and corrections to the Proposition 3.1 proof. The notation guide, sampling clarification, CI-error discussion, and computational-cost analysis make the work easier to understand and assess. These support a limited overall improvement in precision and transparency, while the algorithms and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
